cognitive_validation.rationale: Because the candidate presents no novum-level difference from the empirical world, there is no imaginary science or novel social logic to validate as coherent and immanent.

novum_candidates.description: A private railroad car equipped with its own telegraph instrument and code book, which a bored young woman uses to tap out a distress call by copying Morse code from a fly-leaf.
novum_candidates.estrangement_rationale: No reader-facing estrangement: the telegraph, holdup, and cowboy rescue belong wholly to a realist comic-Western register with no defamiliarizing gap from the empirical world.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The telegraph message driving the rescue does organize much of the plot's causal chain, but centrality alone cannot make a mundane device a novum; hegemony is noted here only for completeness and does not offset the absent novelty.

novelty.rationale: The private telegraph instrument, Morse code, and railroad dispatching are all mundane elements of the author's empirical (early 20th-century, Volstead-era) world. There is no totalizing or world-altering difference from the empirical norm; this is ordinary period technology used in ordinary ways.
